title: ioctl_key_import accepts inbuf_len > keylen without consuming excess
description: ioctl_key_import checks 'if (state->inbuf_len < op.keylen) return -EINVAL' but does NOT check if inbuf_len > op.keylen. When inbuf_len > op.keylen, the import proceeds using only state->inbuf[0..op.keylen-1], which is the documented contract. However, inbuf_clear() is then called unconditionally, zeroizing and freeing ALL inbuf bytes including any bytes beyond keylen. The excess bytes (from a multi-write sequence) are silently discarded with no error. This is probably intentional but is undocumented: the UAPI says 'keylen: number of bytes from the preceding write() to use as the key' implying extra bytes are OK. The actual correctness concern is: if the caller intended those extra bytes for something else, they are silently lost. The DESIGN.md says DO_KDF also uses inbuf, but if a user writes key_bytes || kdf_input and then calls KEY_IMPORT with keylen=key_bytes_len, the kdf_input is silently discarded without error. This is a correctness trap, not a security issue. Trigger: write(key || extra_data) then KEY_IMPORT with keylen=len(key) → extra_data silently discarded, no error returned.
close_reason: fixed: changed inbuf_len < op.keylen to inbuf_len != op.keylen in ioctl_key_import; exact byte count required
